To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effectiveness of feature-based methods for similarity search of 3D object models is strongly dependent on the choice of features and that the choice of features is application-dependent.

(1) 3D similarity queries can be efficiently implemented by using the feature-based approach, (2) the effectiveness of the feature-based approach is comparable to the effectiveness of the shape-based approach, and (3) the effectiveness of 3D similarity searches is comparable to the performance of similarity searches for 2D objects.

(1) the performance of the surveyed algorithms is very dependent on the application domain, (2) the performance of these algorithms is very dependent upon the choice of features and the similarity function, and (3) the performance of some of the methods is very dependent upon a good choice of a feature weighting scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) the development of a general methodology for 3D object retrieval based on feature matching; (2) the design of efficient algorithms to implement the proposed methodology; (3) the design of effective similarity definitions for 3D objects; (4) the design and evaluation of effective similarity definitions; and (5) the design of algorithms that implement the proposed definitions.
the following topics: - Feature-based similarity search in object databases: We survey the literature on feature-based similarity search in databases of 3D shapes.
the design of effective algorithms for 3D object retrieval, based on feature-based methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best method for 3D object retrieval.
no single method can be considered superior in all cases, and that the choice of the method to use is problem dependent.
no method is clearly superior to the others, and that the best method depends on the application domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feature-based similarity search is a viable approach for content-based retrieval, but that the effectiveness of the methods is still not satisfactory.
feature-based similarity search is still an active area of research and there are still many open problems to address, especially in the area of scalability.
feature-based methods have shown to be effective for 3D search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of a feature-based method is highly dependent on the type of 3D data and the similarity metric that it implements.
the performance of 3D similarity retrieval systems is highly dependent on the nature of the application and the characteristics of the database.
the performance of feature-based methods is strongly dependent on the choice of feature descriptors and the similarity measures used.
